summary: Ronan McGovern leads a workshop on fine-tuning Sesame's CSM-1B text-to-speech model to clone a specific voice from YouTube audio. All materials are on the Trellis Research GitHub under AI Worlds Fair 2025. The workshop covers understanding token-based TTS, creating a voice dataset, fine-tuning with Unsloth, and evaluating results. Ronan explains that token-based TTS models predict next audio tokens from text and audio history, using codebooks for discretization. Sesame CSM-1B uses 32 hierarchical tokens per window: the zeroth predicted by a 1B-parameter main transformer, the remaining 31 by a smaller secondary decoder. The practical portion begins with data generation in Colab: downloading YouTube audio via yt-dlp, transcribing with Whisper turbo, and combining segments into up to 30-second chunks. About 50 snippets of 30 seconds each is sufficient for quality improvement. After dataset creation, Ronan installs Unsloth and loads CSM-1B, which fits easily on a T4 (15GB). He demonstrates zero-shot inference (producing random voices due to non-zero temperature) and voice cloning (passing a sample for closer matching), then applies LoRA adapters targeting QVO and MLP linear layers with alpha 16, rank 32, and rescale LoRA, resulting in about 2% trainable parameters. Data formatting uses maximum audio length (~700,000 steps) and text length (587). The trainer uses a virtual batch size of 8, learning rate 2e-4, AdamW 8-bit optimizer, warm-up steps of 3, and constant learning rate for one epoch. Training takes about 10 minutes, with loss falling from ~6.34 to ~3.72 using just under half the GPU memory. Ronan notes the basic setup lacks an eval split and TensorBoard monitoring, both recommended for production use. After training, fine-tuned model inference produces a consistent male voice with Irish accent, though pacing and some pronunciation need improvement. Combining fine-tuning with cloning yields the best results. For better standalone fine-tuning, 500 rows of 30-second audio is recommended. Model saving options include local save, pushing LoRA adapters to Hugging Face, or merging to 16-bit and pushing the full model.

sections.title: Workshop Introduction and Overview
sections.summary: Ronan introduces the workshop on fine-tuning Sesame's CSM-1B TTS model. Materials are on the Trellis Research GitHub. Goals include understanding token-based TTS, creating a voice dataset from YouTube, fine-tuning with Unsloth, and evaluating performance before and after.

sections.title: How Token-Based TTS Models Work
sections.summary: Explains that text models predict next text tokens, while TTS models take text and audio history and predict next audio tokens. Audio is discretized using codebooks trained via encoder-decoder reconstruction. Sesame uses 32 tokens per window: the zeroth predicted by a 1B-parameter main transformer, the other 31 by a smaller secondary decoder.

sections.title: Colab Notebook Setup and Data Generation Overview
sections.summary: Describes the Colab notebook structure with two sections: data generation and fine-tuning/evaluation. Users should connect to a free GPU. Data generation involves picking a single-speaker YouTube video, transcribing with Whisper, and creating a dataset of up to 30-second audio snippets.

sections.title: Data Generation: YouTube Download and Whisper Transcription
sections.summary: Covers installing yt-dlp and Whisper, selecting the turbo Whisper model, running transcription on GPU, and saving results to JSON. Recommends running in Colab to avoid YouTube authentication issues. Manually reviewing and correcting the JSON transcript for misspellings is advised.

sections.title: Dataset Construction and Hugging Face Upload
sections.summary: Explains combining Whisper segments into chunks up to 30 seconds. 41 clips were generated and pushed to Hugging Face. Notes opportunity for improvement: ending rows on full stops using NLTK or regex. Transcription takes a few minutes even for an hour of video.

sections.title: Installing Unsloth and Loading CSM-1B Model
sections.summary: Installs Unsloth with transformers and supporting packages. Loads CSM-1B base model with auto data type (float16 on T4, bfloat16 on newer GPUs). Model is only a few gigabytes and fits easily on T4's 15GB. Sesame models are now supported by transformers natively.

sections.title: Model Architecture and Adapter Strategy
sections.summary: Prints model architecture showing backbone (main transformer), depth decoder (for 31 secondary tokens), and codec model for waveform conversion. Explains only a subset of parameters will be trained: linear layers and adapters, not all parameters, saving memory and speeding training.

sections.title: Zero-Shot Inference and Voice Cloning Demonstration
sections.summary: Demonstrates zero-shot inference producing random speaker voices due to non-zero temperature. Introduces voice cloning as distinct from fine-tuning: passing a sample audio makes output closer to that voice. Loads dataset with audio and text columns (optional source/speaker column defaults to zero). Plays multiple audio samples comparing zero-shot and cloned results.

sections.title: Applying LoRA Adapters and Trainer Data Formatting
sections.summary: Applies LoRA adapters to QVO and MLP linear layers (gate, up, down) with alpha 16, rank 32, and rescale LoRA, which scales learning rate by adapter size. Results in about 2% trainable parameters. Embeddings (LM head, embed tokens) are not trained since tokens are unchanged. Data formatting requires maximum audio length (~700,000 steps) and text length (587) for trainer configuration.

sections.title: Trainer Configuration and Training Execution
sections.summary: Configures the trainer with the processed dataset and model. Uses virtual batch size 8 (actual batch 2), warm-up steps 3, learning rate 2e-4, AdamW 8-bit optimizer, weight decay, and constant learning rate for one epoch. With 41 rows this yields 5 steps per epoch. Training takes about 10 minutes with loss falling from roughly 6.34 to around 3.72, using just under half of the 15GB GPU memory.

sections.title: Training Monitoring and Model Saving Options
sections.summary: Notes the basic setup lacks an eval split; ideally split training set into train and eval to detect overfitting. Recommends TensorBoard for monitoring gradient norm (should be around 1 or less) and losses. After training, model can be saved locally, LoRA adapters pushed to Hugging Face (lightweight), or merged to 16-bit and pushed as full model. Reloading a fine-tuned model uses the fine-tuned model name instead of base model name.

sections.title: Fine-Tuned Model Inference and Evaluation
sections.summary: Runs inference on the fine-tuned model, producing a consistent male voice with Irish accent, removing the randomness of zero-shot inference. Pacing issues noted, potentially improved by better data filtering. Some pronunciation (e.g., 'tuned') still slightly American. Combining cloning with fine-tuning produces the best results, with natural-sounding output including minor natural errors.

sections.title: Workshop Conclusion and Next Steps
sections.summary: Concludes the workshop. For better standalone performance without cloning, aim for 500 rows of 30-second audio. A 30-minute video was sufficient when combining fine-tuning with cloning. Resources available on GitHub at trellis/research/aiworldsfair2025. Future more detailed videos planned on the Trellis Research YouTube channel covering data preparation and hyperparameters in more depth.
